slides.0.title: Analysing global markets and writing the essay
slides.0.subtitle: From facts to a verdict: four steps of a business essay
slides.1.title: Analytical tools
slides.1.highlights.0.title: SWOT
slides.1.highlights.0.content: Strengths and weaknesses (internal), opportunities and threats (external). For a region, strengths are often terroir or varietal identity, threats often climate, tariffs and falling consumption
slides.1.highlights.1.title: Causal chains
slides.1.highlights.1.content: Link facts as “cause → mechanism → result”: e.g. “home demand collapses → surplus cheap wine → high-yield varieties uprooted → turn to quality and exports” (Argentina)
slides.1.highlights.2.title: Using numbers
slides.1.highlights.2.content: Always give numbers with year and source, and compare like with like (volume or value, bottled or bulk). “Stable volume, falling value” or the reverse is itself an argument
slides.1.content: Tools are only the skeleton; marks come from the causes and evidence behind each point.
slides.2.title: Common question types
slides.2.highlights.0.title: Market opportunity questions
slides.2.highlights.0.content: “How should region X develop market Y?”: analyse the market (size, channels, price tiers, regulation), match it to the region’s strengths, then propose feasible strategies and risks
slides.2.highlights.1.title: Industry structure questions
slides.2.highlights.1.content: “The role of co-operatives or large groups in region X”: explain the scale and access they provide and the cost in price pressure and homogeneity (Languedoc, Plaimont, Chile’s top ten wineries)
slides.2.highlights.2.title: Assessment questions
slides.2.highlights.2.content: “Assess the impact of a policy or trend”: give a verdict by dimension (economic, quality, social), with conditions and a time frame, rather than just “good” or “bad”
slides.2.content: Identify the question type before choosing a structure; the same facts are used quite differently in different types.
slides.3.title: A model for assessment essays
slides.3.highlights.0.title: Question
slides.3.highlights.0.content: “Assess the impact of falling consumption on Europe’s volume wine regions.” (about 350 words)
slides.3.highlights.1.title: Facts and mechanism
slides.3.highlights.1.content: Global consumption in 2025 was the lowest since 1961; falling demand → rising stocks → falling grape prices → grubbing-up and distillation (France distilled a tenth of its 2023 crop, and the Languedoc made the largest share of grubbing-up applications)
slides.3.highlights.2.title: Verdict by dimension and conclusion
slides.3.highlights.2.content: Economic: small growers and co-operatives hit hardest; quality: low-value vineyards removed, possibly raising average quality; social: ageing rural population and idle land. Conclusion: short-term pain, long-term restructuring, with success depending on transition funding and market positioning
slides.3.content: A good conclusion is a conditional verdict, not a summary of what came before.
slides.4.componentProps.slide.title: 🧠 Knowledge check
Which parts of SWOT are external?
What is the most important rule when citing export figures?
D. Give year and source and compare like with like
Do not mix volume and value, or bottled and bulk.
What is the best kind of conclusion for an assessment question?
A. A verdict with conditions and a time frame
B. A restatement of every point
D. New facts not yet mentioned
Judge by dimension, then give an overall view.
“Falling demand → rising stocks → falling grape prices → grubbing-up” is what kind of analysis?
Causal chains are the core tool of business essays.
